title: California General Education Transfer Curriculum (Cal-GETC)
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: California General Education Transfer Curriculum (Cal-GETC) Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: demonstrate varied and flexible strategies for generating, drafting, and revising academic writing in multiple genres for multiple communities/audiences.
identify and implement explicit writing and reading strategies useful for navigating audience, purpose, context, genre, language conventions, and varied sources-as-evidence at the college level
analyze, criticize, and generate complex ideas
reason inductively and deductively
identify the assumptions upon which particular conclusions depend
reflect critically on one’s own thought processes
respond appropriately to texts, with attention to their intended audience, purpose, and social context
distinguish knowledge from belief and fact from judgment
recognize common logical errors or fallacies of language and thought
evaluate sources with respect to their relevance, reliability, and appropriateness to the rhetorical context
analyze and construct arguments, especially in research and written work that attends appropriately to audience, purpose, context, genre, and language conventions.
recognize the theoretical foundations of creating and sharing knowledge, including the canons of rhetoric and the Aristotelian proofs of ethos, pathos, and logos
find, critically examine, and use supporting materials from primary and secondary sources for credibility, accuracy, and relevance in their speeches and presentations
conceptualize and effectively use compelling arguments in support of a guiding thesis and organizational pattern appropriate for the audience, occasion, and across a variety of contexts
adhere to ethical communication practices which include truthfulness, accuracy, honesty, and reason as essential to the integrity of communication
demonstrate rhetorical sensitivity to diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging, and accessibility
deliver a variety of well-prepared faculty-supervised, faculty-evaluated speeches delivered to a live audience (one to many) using effective delivery techniques
employ effective verbal and nonverbal practices while delivering a speech and managing communication apprehension
listen critically to provide constructive criticism to peers
apply rhetorical principles to analyze historical and contemporary public discourse
participate in quantitative reasoning and have the capacity to critique quantitative arguments
demonstrate understanding of major civilizations and cultures, both Western and non-Western, through the study of philosophy, language, literature, religion, and the fine arts.
analyze and appreciate works aesthetic and cultural importance in the fine arts.
recognize the contributions to knowledge, civilization, and society that have been made by men and women as well as members of various ethnic or cultural groups
analyze and appreciate works of philosophical, historical, literary, and cultural importance.
explain the perspectives and research methods of the social and behavioral sciences.
recognize and appreciate the contributions and perspectives of men, women and of ethnic and other minorities and a comparative perspective on both Western and non-Western societies
Analyze problems and issues in the social and behavioral sciences in their contemporary, historical, and geographic settings.

demonstrate understanding of basic scientific concepts of the physical and biological aspects of the world as well as an understanding of science as a human endeavor including its limitations and power.
use experimental methodology, the testing of hypotheses, investigation, and the process of systematic questioning and assessment, rather than the recall of facts, data, and events.

Analyze and articulate concepts such as race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, ethno-centrism, eurocentrism, white supremacy, self-determination, liberation, decolonization, sovereignty, imperialism, settler colonialism, and antiracism as analyzed in any one or more of the following: Native American Studies, African American Studies, Asian American Studies, and Latina and Latino American Studies

Apply theory and knowledge produced by Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities to describe the critical events, histories, cultures, intellectual traditions, contributions, lived-experiences and social struggles of those groups with a particular emphasis on agency and group affirmation.

Critically analyze the intersection of race and racism as they relate to class, gender, sexuality, religion, spirituality, national origin, immigration status, ability, tribal citizenship, sovereignty, language, and/or age in Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities.

Critically review how struggle, resistance, racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation, as experienced and enacted by Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans and/or Latina and Latino Americans are relevant to current and structural issues such as communal, national, international, and transnational politics as, for example, in immigration, reparations, settler-colonialism, multiculturalism, language policies.

Describe and actively engage with anti-racist and anti-colonial issues and the practices and movements in Native American, African American, Asian American and/or Latina and Latino communities and a just and equitable society.

notes: The award is the Cal-GETC pattern itself, so its GE areas are recorded as blocks; ge_pattern left null because no separate GE pattern is named for a degree.

No total for the certificate is printed; area-level figures (Area 1 9 units, Area 2 3 units, Area 3 6 units, Area 4 6 units, Area 5 7-9 units) are in area intro text, and each group heading says 'N units minimum'; block stated left null.
Catalog prints ARTH and THA codes with a space (e.g., ARTH V01, THA V28) and CDEV C1000 with a space; treated as matching closed-list ARTHV01, THAV28, CDEVC1000.
ENGL C1003 appears in both 1B and 3B; PHIL V10, ANTH V04, CHST V01, CHST V03 and several HIST courses appear in both 3B and Area 4; listed in each block where printed.
Area 5: one course from 5A and one from 5B, at least one including a laboratory (5C); each 5A/5B course must be at least 3 units. 5C lists lab-inclusive courses that also appear in 5A/5B.
Area 4 requires two courses from two different disciplines.
PHYS V01 (Elementary Physics, 5) is printed in 5A and 5C but not in the closed list.
Outcomes list includes Area 6 (Ethnic Studies) outcomes, but the requirements tab prints no Area 6 course list; ETHS courses from the closed list are not in the text.

Outcomes were printed with area labels (1A., 1B., 3A or 3B., etc.) which were removed as list labels; text otherwise copied as printed. The outcomes are printed for the program as a whole and the certificate shares them.
Part 2: The award is itself the Cal-GETC pattern, so its area course lists are recorded as blocks; ge_pattern left null because no separate GE pattern is required on top of these requirements.

Part 2: No total units for the certificate is printed in the text; total_units left null. Area-level totals (Area 1: 9 units; Area 2: 3; Area 3: 6; Area 4: 6; Area 5: 7-9) and per-group '(N units minimum)' figures are minimums, not recorded as block stated totals.

Part 2: Area 6 (Ethnic Studies) requirements are not printed in the requirements text, though the outcomes list includes Area 6 outcomes; the requirements table may be cut off. ETHS V01, V02, V14 therefore unplaced.
Part 2: Area 4 requires two courses from two different disciplines; recorded as choose 2 courses.

Part 2: Area 5: one course from 5A and one from 5B, at least one of which must include a laboratory (5C); 5C is recorded as choose 1 but may be satisfied by a 5A/5B course that includes a lab rather than an additional course. Each 5A/5B course must be at least 3 units.
Part 2: PHYS V01 (Elementary Physics, 5) appears in 5A and 5C but is not in the closed list; recorded as catalog_addition.
Part 2: SOCI C1000 and ASTR C1001/C1001L are printed with a space; the closed list stores SOCIC1000, ASTRC1001, ASTRC1001L, treated as the same courses.

Part 2: Outcomes are printed as one program outcomes list for the award, each prefixed with a Cal-GETC area label (1A, 1B, 1C, 2, 3A, 3B, '3A or 3B', 4, 5, 6); those labels were omitted as list labels.
Part 2: Courses in Areas 1-3 and some Area 4 courses belong to part 1 of this record; those blocks are listed empty here.
